conditions: An evaluation is admitted on its exact subject, basis and predicate.

grounding.quote:
Every admitted constraint evaluation returns the shared
[result record](FOUNDATIONS.md#result-algebra) on its exact subject, basis and
predicate. All five core verdicts are available when evaluating an in-domain
subject. A request outside that domain returns `out_of_frame` at the invocation
boundary; it is not forged into an in-domain judgment. Performance and effect state remain separate
coordinates. An omitted or unperformed evaluation is never a positive result.

The judgment decisions below are domain refinements. `satisfied` maps to the
positive decision, which is first in each row; `invalid_basis` maps only to
`invalid_basis`. The constraint table fixes other mappings. Keep the original
decision, constraint predicate, evidence, residuals and stop in the shared
return. The table does not define a second aggregation or result algebra.

constraints.statement: Use the shared result record, not a second result or aggregation algebra; retain decision, exact predicate, evidence, residuals and stop, with performance and effects separate. All five core verdicts are available in-domain; an outside-domain invocation returns out_of_frame without inventing an in-domain judgment. Omitted/unperformed evaluation is never positive. satisfied maps to the first positive decision in each judgment domain; invalid_basis maps only to invalid_basis. valid/admitted/ready satisfy only their respective predicate, not the external intended outcome. Missing decisive evidence retains indeterminate; demonstrated false predicates remain falsified even when their domain decision is refused, stale, unauthorized, out_of_scope or stale-frontier hold. In-domain event_scope_compatible falsification is not invocation-boundary out_of_frame. Every inherited Judgment retains unchanged subject id/digest, evaluator, authority, evidence, provenance and decision; stops/residuals come from its kind, not prose inference.

grounding.quote:
| `effect_readiness` | `EffectSubject` | `ready`, `stale`, `unauthorized`, `hold`, `invalid_basis` | exact pre-observation, invocation, operation, grant, territory, and invalidation state | stale yields `hold` plus `stale_currentness` and re-observation; unauthorized yields `refusal` and no dispatch |
| `transition_evaluation` | `TransitionSubject` | `satisfied`, `falsified`, `partial`, `indeterminate`, `refused`, `invalid_basis` | exact pre/post observations, intended outcome, disposition, and bounded effect evidence | partial yields `partial_effect`; indeterminate retains `hold` plus a declared residual; refused yields `refusal` |
| `frontier_projection` | `Projection` | `admitted`, `hold`, `gap`, `refused`, `invalid_basis` | exact projection/frontier ids and digests, complete members, basis, precedence law, boundary, and residuals | stale frontier retains `hold` plus `stale_frontier`; unresolved lineage retains `gap`; re-enter with a new projection |

constraints.statement: Closed judgment contracts: model_validation over OccurrenceModelSubject has {valid, hold, refused, invalid_basis}, requires exact model id/digest, profile basis and typed populations; unresolved refs retain gap until repaired. occurrence_admission over Occurrence has {admitted, hold, refused, invalid_basis}, requires exact id/digest and resolved pre-existing seeds; missing seeds retain hold/unresolved_cause and require a new complete candidate. event_admission over FrameworkEvent has {admitted, hold, refused, invalid_basis, out_of_scope}, requires exact event id/digest, payload digest, scope authority and source frontier; unresolved scope retains hold/unresolved_scope, incompatible scope refuses. claim_admission over RelationClaim has {admitted, hold, refused, invalid_basis}, requires exact id/digest, endpoints, qualifiers, claimant authority and current frontier; unresolved cause retains hold/unresolved_cause; established staleness falsifies admission with hold/stale_frontier and requires a new current-frontier claim. semantic_cut_admission over SemanticAdmissionCut has {admitted, hold, refused, invalid_basis}, requires the exact seven-member cut and source/successor equality joins; conjoin claim/event judgments and joins, retaining hold/unresolved_cause naming missing, held or unauthenticated support slots; established staleness falsifies with hold/stale_frontier; unchanged-subject re-entry rules apply. effect_readiness over EffectSubject has {ready, stale, unauthorized, hold, invalid_basis}, requires exact pre-observation, invocation, operation, grant, territory and invalidation; stale retains hold/stale_currentness and re-observation, unauthorized retains refusal/no dispatch. transition_evaluation over TransitionSubject has {satisfied, falsified, partial, indeterminate, refused, invalid_basis}, requires exact pre/post observations, intended outcome, disposition and bounded effect evidence; partial retains partial_effect, indeterminate retains hold/declared residual, refused retains refusal. frontier_projection over Projection has {admitted, hold, gap, refused, invalid_basis}, requires exact projection/frontier ids/digests, complete members, basis, precedence, boundary and residuals; stale retains hold/stale_frontier, unresolved lineage retains gap, re-entry constructs a new projection.

grounding.quote:
| `pre_effect_current` | `EffectSubject` | `effect_readiness` | `stale` plus `hold` and `stale_currentness` | `hold` plus `stale_currentness` |
| `operation_grant_contains_effect` | `EffectSubject` | `effect_readiness` | `unauthorized` plus `refusal` | `hold` plus `unobserved_subject_state` |
| `event_scope_compatible` | `FrameworkEvent` | `event_admission` | `out_of_scope` plus `refusal` | `hold` plus `unresolved_scope` |
| `frontier_complete` | `Projection` | `frontier_projection` | `refused` plus `refusal`; established stale frontier retains `hold` plus `stale_frontier` | `hold` plus `unresolved_cause` |
| `transition_subject_complete` | `TransitionSubject` | `transition_evaluation` | `refused` plus `refusal`; intended-outcome basis diagnosis below | `indeterminate` plus `unobserved_subject_state` |

constraints.statement: identity_dependency_acyclic, occurrence_causation_acyclic and event_causation_acyclic use OccurrenceModelSubject/model_validation; occurrence_seed_complete uses Occurrence/occurrence_admission: each falsification maps refused/refusal and each indeterminate maps hold/unresolved_cause. relation_claim_admissible uses RelationClaim/claim_admission; semantic_cut_complete uses SemanticAdmissionCut/semantic_cut_admission; frontier_complete uses Projection/frontier_projection: falsification maps refused/refusal except established stale frontier retains hold/stale_frontier; indeterminate maps hold/unresolved_cause, with the cut naming the undecided slot/join. pre_effect_current uses EffectSubject/effect_readiness: falsified maps stale/hold/stale_currentness, indeterminate maps hold/stale_currentness. operation_grant_contains_effect uses the same subject/judgment: falsified maps unauthorized/refusal, indeterminate maps hold/unobserved_subject_state. event_scope_compatible uses FrameworkEvent/event_admission: falsified maps out_of_scope/refusal, indeterminate maps hold/unresolved_scope. transition_subject_complete uses TransitionSubject/transition_evaluation: falsified maps refused/refusal with the separate intended-outcome basis diagnosis; indeterminate maps indeterminate/unobserved_subject_state.

grounding.quote:
Source-frontier currentness is a material join of claim admission, cut
admission and frontier projection. Established staleness falsifies that exact
predicate; its `hold` decision with cause `stale_frontier` prevents use and
requires reconstruction. Unknown currentness is indeterminate. The word
`hold` alone decides neither case. A missing material scope or capability on
an in-domain subject retains core `out_of_frame`, stop `out_of_scope` and
`unresolved_cause` naming the missing relation. Its decision is `hold`, or
`indeterminate` for `transition_evaluation`, whose domain has no `hold` value.
Re-enter with a capable frame under the original subject/basis or retain the
stop. These diagnostic rules apply to every judgment kind without adding a
second verdict domain.

constraints.statement: Bind transition evaluation to the exact intended-outcome predicate on declared pre/post observations. A partial decision retains evidence/provenance reason unfulfilled → falsified or unknown → indeterminate; missing required reason/support also yields indeterminate without inventing completion or erasing counterevidence. These are reason cases, not new kinds; keep partial observations and cause, and assess effects separately because failed outcome does not imply no effect. Established source-frontier staleness falsifies the exact currentness join, retaining hold/stale_frontier to prevent use and require reconstruction; unknown currentness is indeterminate. For every in-domain judgment, missing material scope/capability retains core out_of_frame, stop out_of_scope and unresolved_cause naming the missing relation, with hold decision except transition_evaluation uses indeterminate; re-enter with a capable frame under original subject/basis or keep the stop. transition_subject_complete is a prerequisite, not the outcome predicate: demonstrated incompleteness preserves its counterexample and refused decision, while an outcome evaluation unable to use that subject is invalid_basis; merely unacquired information leaves outcome indeterminate/unobserved_subject_state. grounding.quote:
| `unobserved_subject_state` | `SubjectBinding` | acquire a bounded observation or retain hold |
| `partial_effect` | `EffectInvocation` | acquire post-observation and explicit disposition |

grounding.quote:
Two applications of one traversal over one subject are two occurrences. A
retry or continuation creates a fresh occurrence only when it reapplies the
traversal. A controller step, observation, wait, or correlation record does not
become an occurrence merely because it happens later.

For composition, every retained bracketed traversal application under AC-016
has its own occurrence. If a declared composite traversal is itself applied,
it also has one aggregate occurrence. Each component application relates to
that aggregate through `component_of_occurrence`; that relation is not material

provenance, and stops required by AC-016 remain explicit.

An event does not inherit the candidate's authority. Materialization cannot

Retain component judgments/joins under their own identities. Only exact admitted j_c, j_e and j_a admit the whole cut. Claim, judgments, event, relation and cut have distinct identities/authority; construction does not admit, judgment does not rewrite, event inherits no candidate authority, and materialization cannot alter accepted relation kind/endpoints/qualifiers/basis. j_c, j_e and j_a respectively have claim_admission, event_admission and semantic_cut_admission kinds, bind c/e/a ids and SHA-256 digests of canonical subject bytes, and retain complete inherited context, owner, scope, basis, evaluator, authority, predicate, verdict, decision, performance, effects, evidence, residuals, provenance and decision-time. conditions: corrects_event(new, existing) is asserted.

grounding.quote:
`corrects_event(new, existing)` retains both immutable events. Correction
changes later projection through an explicit selection law. It does not delete,
rewrite, or retrospectively re-identify the corrected fact.

constraints.statement: Retain both immutable events. Correction changes later projection only through an explicit selection law and cannot delete, rewrite or retrospectively re-identify the corrected fact.

grounding.quote:
Each is acyclic under its own typed relation. Cause is established only by an
admitted causal claim under competent authority and evidence. Timestamp,
ordinal, adjacency, containment, common subject, shared actor, correlation,

constraints.statement: Cause requires an admitted causal claim with competent authority and evidence. Timestamp, ordinal, adjacency, containment, common subject, shared actor, correlation and arrival order create no cause. Each identity/causal graph is independently acyclic. Opposing differently typed lineage edges, such as support and correction, are lawful; an untyped-union cycle is causal only if a declared causal subgraph itself cycles.

conditions: A projection uses a declared precedence coordinate to select current truth.

A projection may use a declared precedence coordinate to select current truth.
The coordinate, comparison law, basis, and admitting authority are explicit.
The coordinate orders eligible facts; it does not gain semantic, admission,
causal, or decision authority.

conditions: A domain effect is proposed for dispatch.
exceptions: An adopting Product may replace exact territory equality only through an explicit authority-owned containment relation in its compatible signature.

grounding.quote:
The exact `OperationKind` object therefore closes the grant over both kind and
contract. A grant cannot authorize a same-labelled operation instance carrying
a different contract, target sort, invalidated kind, or unresolved kind ref.

An adopting Product may replace exact territory equality only through an
explicit, authority-owned containment relation in its compatible signature.
Nominal kind equality, a role label, executor access, or broad workspace access
does not satisfy the grant.

constraints.statement: F_P/F_D/F_H classification alone neither identifies, authorizes nor executes the operation. Apply Contract application to unchanged EffectSubject immediately before dispatch, using an owner-issued grant for subject binding, operation kind and territory; profile construction/occurrence admission provide none. Bind invocation.operation_ref = operation.id; operation_of_kind target = operation.operation_kind_ref; targets_subject target = operation.subject_binding_ref; authorized_by(invocation) target = invocation.operation_grant_ref = grant.id; operation, grant and occurrence subject bindings equal; operation kind belongs to grant.allowed_operation_kind_refs; operation contract equals the exact OperationKind object's contract; operation, invocation and grant allowed territory refs equal subject to the stated exception. Wrong contract/target sort, invalidated kind or unresolved kind cannot be authorized by matching labels. Role labels, executor access and workspace access do not satisfy grants. Only ready dispatches; stale or unauthorized never dispatches. Immediately pre-dispatch, apply declared currentness/invalidation law; stale pre-observation or grant requires re-observation plus a new readiness subject/judgment, or stop. grounding.quote:
A dispatch followed by lost transport without resolving observation cannot
become `no_effect`, `refused_effect` or `completed_effect`. Missing
post-observation remains an explicit residual and prevents a complete profile
disposition from being manufactured. Observation is required before any action
that depends on whether that effect happened, including a repeat.
An unauthorized mutation is still an actual effect. Lack of permission cannot
establish `not_started` or justify a `refused_effect` disposition that conceals
observed or uncertain mutation.

constraints.statement: Closed dispositions: no_effect has no dispatched invocation and records no attempted domain effect, whether unrequested or stopped before dispatch; completed_effect binds one dispatched invocation, bounded post-observation and sufficient evidence; partial_effect binds one dispatched invocation, bounded post-observation/evidence, partial_effect residual/stop and explicit re-entry before further effect; refused_effect binds the refused attempt, refusal stop and evidence no mutation began. invokes_effect exists iff concrete dispatch occurred. Immutable invocation has no future disposition; later EffectDisposition does not rewrite it. Shared effects follow observations: no_effect maps not_requested only for established effect-free scope, not mere absent request; requested-but-stopped maps not_started only with authenticated non-dispatch evidence, otherwise claimed disposition is unadmitted and requested effect unknown. Supported refused_effect maps not_started; observed completed_effect maps completed. Domain partial_effect keeps incomplete disposition/re-entry while core observation/join law classifies the full material boundary, preserving observed parts, reversals and unknown remainder; it may retain core partial, reverted or unknown and adds no authority/kind. Local rollback cannot conceal irreversible messages. Lost transport after dispatch cannot manufacture no_effect/refused_effect/completed_effect; missing post-observation remains residual and requires observation before any dependent action or repeat. Unauthorized mutation remains actual effect and cannot be concealed as not_started/refused_effect. Begun effects lacking complete disposition retain explicit partial_effect and require bounded post-observation.

conditions: The stable subject-binding authority remains unchanged.

grounding.quote:
Apply [workspace and context](FOUNDATIONS.md#workspace-and-context) with
`W` as the external reality carrier and `SubjectBinding` as its stable
binding. A later traversal application observes the then-current `W` while
that authority remains unchanged. Occurrence records, checkpoints, events,
projections, caches and models are accounts of that subject, not substitutes.

conditions: A traversal is reapplied.

grounding.quote:
Iteration does not mutate an earlier occurrence. Each traversal reapplication
mints a fresh immutable occurrence over the evolving subject. The admitted
occurrence and event history is therefore append-only even when the external
subject changes repeatedly.

constraints.statement: Mint a fresh immutable occurrence over the evolving subject; do not mutate earlier occurrences. Admitted occurrence/event history remains append-only despite repeated external changes.

grounding.quote:
Projection judgment applies
[Faithful projection](TRANSFORMATION_LIBRARY.md#faithful-projection) to
one unchanged `Projection` identity/digest and its exact `EventFrontier`.
The source binding is that frontier's complete event member set, exact basis
and declared precedence law. The target interpretation is the declared
projection rule with its selected relations, boundaries and residuals.
These bindings are the profile's completeness and fidelity criteria.

Bind complete event membership, exact basis and declared precedence to the declared rule, selected relations, boundaries and residuals. New events require new frontiers; old projections never silently advance. Latest-only summaries do not prove completeness. Competing corrections, unresolved scope, missing causal inputs and stale basis retain residuals/stops according to the selected projection law.

constraints.statement: Every material operation/judgment applies Contract application's authority condition to an existing owner-issued grant for its domain role. Every clause ref is an absolute URI whose base is the exact publication
`member_uri`; only its fragment differs. The calculus clause ref is an absolute
URI inside the exact calculus publication basis. Relative paths, mutable source
URIs, missing fragments, duplicate refs, or a ref outside those two exact
publication members refuse the signature.

They define the closed sorts, fields, values, relations, constraints, judgments, residuals, stops and exact functor refs; sort duplicate-free by ascending unsigned UTF-16 code units. All refs are absolute exact-publication addresses; calculus ref belongs inside its exact calculus member; relative/mutable paths, absent fragments, duplicates or refs outside the two exact members refuse. profile_member_sha256 equals publication member digest. Signature identity is sha256(JCS(signature)) using RFC 8785. Every digest is lowercase sha256:<64-hex>. release_uri is immutable absolute stdo://releases/v<version>-rc.<positive-ordinal>/; member_uri is exactly that plus standards/TRAVERSAL_OCCURRENCE_PROFILE.md. grounding.quote:
Resolve the historical byte predicates from complete successor-owned
[derivation verification material](IDENTITY_METHOD.md#derivation-verification-material)
when present in the exact publication manifest. Verify the material's member
digest, its source-member pins, reconstructed historical digests and complete
principle-ref population before admitting the imported basis. The original
historical manifest and clause identities remain distinct from the successor
publication and external judgments. This evidence resolution requires neither
the predecessor Install nor historical retrieval; absent or defective material
retains the refusal conditions above.

Its manifest digest resolves exact bytes containing calculus member path/digest once; resolved member matches; calculus clause ref is exact member URI plus #core-signature. A distinct predecessor manifest resolves sorted duplicate-free principle_refs inside its declared release, exactly the absolute expansion of every derivation address, neither subset nor invented list; the edition described here has fourteen. Each predecessor member's exact digest occurs once and each fragment resolves one heading under the semantic-address rule. Shape-only strings, unresolved basis, manifest/member mismatch, missing/extra principles, invented/absent fragments, unbound predecessor bytes or same-carrier derivation refuse. When complete successor-owned derivation verification material is present in the exact manifest, verify its digest, source pins, reconstructed historical digests and complete principles; keep historical manifest/clause identities distinct from successor publication and external judgments. This needs neither predecessor Install nor historical retrieval; absent/defective material retains refusal conditions. Profile publication uses the same manifest/member rule. Mutable source paths, strategy posts, implementations and consumer mappings cannot substitute for either basis/publication identity. Any calculus-basis, signature-ref, closed-signature or member-byte change mints a new profile basis; supersession needs external Product/release judgment and never silently advances an earlier basis.

constraints.statement: The profile changes neither pure a_c nor pure Reference Frame law; is not mandatory for every symbolic model; supplies no concrete subject/workspace ontology, process/traversal/retry/continuation/closure engine, event store/log schema/projection implementation/state carrier, mutation/admission/evaluation/decision authority, or prospective-frame/sensor-population profile; guarantees neither occurrence ownership of every event nor acyclicity of every typed-lineage graph.

conditions: Review or qualification of profile conformance is undertaken.

grounding.quote:
Review and qualification cover at least:

1. instantiation under one exact `a_c` basis, the exact eight-member
   `RecordKind_ac` population function, and closed reference domains without
   inherited-field shadowing;

constraints.statement: Review/qualification covers at least: one exact a_c basis, exact eight-member RecordKind_ac population, closed references/no inherited shadowing; inherited families/direct coordinates/disjoint local-external identities; complete seeds and every mirroring relation/future result-event refusal; first event without fictional predecessor; distinct candidate/judgment/event/relation/cut/cut-judgment identities and unchanged digests; idempotent/refused duplicates; cycles in each identity/causal graph; lawful opposing support/correction; closed event kinds/payloads/digests/scope/bindings and no fabricated event_for; separation of functor/traversal/operation-kind/operation-instance/executor/actor/grant/invocation/target/territory; missing/stale/mismatched/out-of-territory grants; all four effect dispositions; external reality conservation; fresh reapplication identities; component/aggregate occurrences; stale observation/grant-currentness refusal; incomplete admission batches including missing/non-admitted cut judgment and unequal claim/event/cut frontiers; frontier completeness/staleness/correction selection; non-causation by timestamp/ordinal/adjacency/containment/correlation; absent adoption/incomplete mapping refusal; exact JCS/kind/schema/immutable URI/digest/calculus address/unique-member basis reconstruction. Examples/checkers establish only claims actually evaluated and become neither occurrence engines nor semantic authority.

conditions: Within the adopted UX surface.

grounding.quote:
Within its adopted surface, apply
[Contract application](TRANSFORMATION_LIBRARY.md#contract-application) at the
typed input, command-dispatch, replay and closure boundaries. Bind the exact
Product contracts, State/Msg/Update/Cmd/Sub algebras, current owning state,
evidence and actual effect/decision grants. Emitting a command supplies no
Product-truth or runtime-continuation authority.

The arguments below use [F1–F6](FOUNDATIONS.md#foundational-commitments)
within the surface governed by this profile. The Product supplies admitted
truth and action contracts; the UX renders that truth, requests changes and
receives data across seams it may not control. Stacks offer different state and
effect mechanisms. Those instance conditions motivate explicit contracts but
do not derive TEA, an accessibility standard or one implementation stack.

constraints.statement: UX maps Foundations, Transformation Library and Design Module; its adoption/default-coverage/scaffold/exemption clauses bound its surface. Spec and Ticket retain constitutional process/work lifecycle; ODD and World Model retain separate carrier/domain meanings. Contract application at typed ingress, dispatch, replay and closure binds exact Product contracts, State/Msg/Update/Cmd/Sub, current owning state, evidence and real grants. Command emission grants no Product truth or continuation. F1–F6 motivate explicit contracts but do not derive TEA, accessibility standards or a stack; those are this method's domain policy. Working prototypes do not authorize exceptions or prove release fitness. Owning state differs from projection; loss-on-unmount exposes material state. Commands, dispatch and observed effects differ; failed responses cannot prove no mutation or authorize blind repeat. UI types/handlers cannot replace missing carriers; compile-time assertions do not admit untrusted input. Replay proves traces, not unknown-effect completion. Accessibility duties are independent of replay. Escrow defers proof without completing it; Ticket owns sprint-close classification/eligibility. Applicable Design Module and UX obligations conjoin at their actual closure consumer using the shared result record/conjunction.

conditions: The UX method governs the surface.
exceptions: The expressly bounded view-local-ephemera permission is retained in ux_local_state_latitude.

grounding.quote:
The view is not a state owner.

Stateful local mutation in views, two-way bindings without action emission, and effect-handlers-as-controllers are method violations even when they are conventionally accepted in the surrounding ecosystem.

constraints.statement: The method makes 'using UX_METHOD, build this UI surface' precise through TEA: pure typed-state View, pure typed-message reductions, reducer-described effects interpreted at a declared membrane and runtime-owned lifecycle. The view owns neither material state nor continuation. Local stateful view mutation, two-way binding without action emission and effect handlers acting as controllers violate the method despite ecosystem convention.

conditions: A product, ticket, design module or review adopts the method for the surface.
exceptions: Before implementation in an ambiguous case, satisfy the stricter interpretation, reprice through the governing constitutional method, or record a scoped design-module exemption.

grounding.quote:
When a product, ticket, design module, or review adopts this method for a UX
surface, `UX_METHOD.md` is the sole UX realization authority for that surface.

Project-local ADRs may choose the stack. They may not weaken the process model.

Existing code, component-library convention, screenshots, comments, design
history, prototype behavior, and generated artifacts are evidence only. They do
not override this method.

If this method appears ambiguous in a concrete case, the surface fails closed:
the work must either satisfy the stricter interpretation, reprice through the
governing constitutional method, or record a scoped exemption in the design
module before implementation proceeds.

constraints.statement: UX_METHOD is the sole UX realization authority for the covered surface. Local ADRs may choose stacks but cannot weaken the process. Existing code, conventions, screenshots, comments, history, prototypes and generated artifacts are evidence, not overrides. Ambiguity fails closed until one stated exit is met.

grounding.quote:
- when a module realizes a UX surface, both `DESIGN_MODULE_METHOD.md` and `UX_METHOD.md` apply
- when a module realizes a non-UX surface, only `DESIGN_MODULE_METHOD.md` applies
- when an ODD product publishes a projection / query surface that includes UX (`§10` of `ODD_METHOD.md`), `UX_METHOD.md` governs that surface's realization

The composition rule is:

- `ODD_METHOD.md` answers what graph-native shape the product takes
- `DESIGN_MODULE_METHOD.md` answers what realization discipline the modules follow
- `UX_METHOD.md` answers what additional discipline UX surfaces follow

constraints.statement: UX modules apply both Design Module and UX methods; non-UX modules apply Design Module only. ODD projection/query surfaces containing UX are governed by UX realization law. ODD determines graph-native shape, Design Module determines module discipline and UX adds UX discipline.

conditions: A Msg changes Product truth.

grounding.quote:
Such a message must map to one admitted product carrier:

- an `AssetSurface` action
- a published graph function or lawful graph-function composition
- a workorder, job, or runtime command admitted by the product's design
- an ABG event or command boundary where ABG is the runtime authority
- another typed product contract named by the design module

The UX layer must not become the hidden constructive carrier. If no admitted
carrier exists for a product-truth-changing message, the UX surface is blocked
until the carrier is authored or the requirement is repriced.

constraints.statement: Map each Product-truth-changing message to one admitted AssetSurface action, published graph function/lawful composition, design-admitted workorder/job/runtime command, ABG boundary where ABG owns runtime authority, or another typed Product contract named in the design module. UX cannot become a hidden constructive carrier. Missing carrier blocks the surface until authored or requirement repriced.

exceptions: Declare Sub when the surface subscribes to external or runtime events.

grounding.quote:
Each `Cmd` declaration names:

- the effect kind
- the typed input payload
- the admitted carrier or external boundary it targets
- the typed outcome `Msg` family returned to the reducer, including every
  observed or unresolved effect case possible under the command contract (§6)
- the reason and observation carried by each case; a success/failure label alone
  does not establish completion or absence of effects
- any deterministic correlation key required for replay

The reducer is pure. It does not perform I/O, log to side channels, or mutate global state. Effects scheduled by `Cmd` are interpreted by the runtime at the effect membrane (see §6).

constraints.statement: State changes through typed Msg applied by pure Update. Declare State, Msg, Update:(Msg,State)→(State,Cmd), Cmd and applicable Sub. Each Cmd names effect kind, typed payload, admitted carrier/external target, every possible observed/unresolved typed outcome Msg, each case's reason/observation, and needed deterministic replay correlation key. Success/failure labels alone establish neither completion nor no effect. Reducer performs no I/O, side-channel logging or global mutation. Runtime interprets Cmds at the membrane. grounding.quote:

Selection emits contract-consistent Context/equivalent updates. Writes use the action registry, not direct files/services. Shared typed contracts are front/back-end ground truth. grounding.quote:
State transitions flow through declared `Msg` actions interpreted by the reducer. A view does not:

- decide on its own what the next state will be after a user event
- chain multiple state updates locally without emitting them as separate `Msg` values
- carry hidden inter-event state in refs, closures, or module-level variables

If a view appears to need a multi-step local state machine, that state machine belongs in the reducer as part of `State`, with explicit `Msg` transitions between phases. The view becomes a pure projection of which phase it is in.

The discipline test is the **Msg-replay test**: can you replay the view's behavior by replaying its `Msg` log against an empty `State`? If the answer is no, continuation has leaked into the view.

constraints.statement: The source cites ODD §11.5A as ABG-owned continuation with Product as bounded-step subsystem and applies its UX twin: View does not own state continuation. It cannot independently choose next state, chain local updates without separate Msg, or hide inter-event state in refs/closures/module variables. grounding.quote:

completion of the underlying effect. A demonstrated expected-state or command
mismatch, or a demonstrated dependency on any source excluded by this replay
contract, is `falsified`; a
proof not run retains `not_performed` and cannot satisfy the predicate.
Missing decisive trace is `indeterminate`; an unusable fixture or governing
basis is `invalid_basis`; an interaction outside the declared assessment domain

Correctness must not depend on unrepresented DOM state; mutable refs/module variables/closures/timers/handler memory; network/file results bypassing Msg; or local state affecting behavior after unmount/replay. Expected state/commands/returns under declared conditions satisfy replay, not underlying unknown-effect completion. Demonstrated mismatch/excluded dependency falsifies; unrun proof is not_performed and cannot satisfy; missing decisive trace is indeterminate; unusable fixture/basis invalid_basis; outside-domain interaction out_of_frame. grounding.quote:
### Fully Qualified Naming Is Mandatory

Many cross-domain failures are preventable naming collisions.

Fully qualified naming removes aliasing so the remaining hard work is real
semantic transformation.

constraints.statement: Use fully qualified naming to remove preventable naming collisions/aliasing before semantic transformation; naming does not itself resolve semantic transformation.

grounding.quote:
API contracts and schema contracts are projections over the world model.

They are useful because they publish structure and function. They are not the
highest semantic authority.

constraints.statement: API/schema contracts project world-model structure and function; they are not highest semantic authority.

grounding.quote:
The canonical published entity cut should remain semantic and bounded.

Probability belongs in uncertainty, ranking, anomaly, and alignment overlays,
not in the ontological identity of the published object itself.

That overlay may include:

- correspondence candidates
- confidence and ranking
- ambiguity registers
- anomaly and surprise signals
- candidate mappings or treatment suggestions

The overlay is useful because it lets probabilistic reasoning operate over a
governed semantic substrate rather than over detached strings, schemas, or raw
tables.

But the overlay is not the same thing as published semantic truth.

Accepted semantic treatments, published domain artifacts, and compiled
deterministic execution artifacts remain distinct from probabilistic overlays.

constraints.statement: Canonical entity cuts should stay semantic/bounded. Probability belongs in uncertainty/ranking/anomaly/alignment overlays, not published-object ontological identity. Overlays may include correspondence candidates, confidence/rankings, ambiguity, anomaly/surprise and candidate mappings/treatments. They support reasoning over the governed substrate but remain distinct from published truth, accepted treatments, domain artifacts and deterministic execution artifacts.

conditions: Use the strongest available explanatory surfaces.
exceptions: Code availability is never a prerequisite for comprehension.

grounding.quote:
Preferred hierarchy:

1. realized system behavior and emitted records or events
2. source code, rules, and configuration when available
3. interfaces and schemas
4. large-scale observational data evidence
5. documentation, catalogs, and operator testimony

Code is a high-fidelity explanatory surface when available.

Realized behavior remains the broader truth surface because some systems are
proprietary, partially visible, or only intelligible through their outputs and
effects.

The method therefore never depends on code availability as a prerequisite for
comprehension.

constraints.statement: Preferred evidence order is realized behavior/emitted records/events; available code/rules/configuration; interfaces/schemas; large-scale observational data; documentation/catalogs/operator testimony. Code is high-fidelity when available, but realized behavior is broader because systems may be proprietary/partial/output-only. Preserve the preference rather than making unavailable code a prerequisite.

conditions: A traced observation is assessed as a qualified semantic claim.

grounding.quote:
Return that exact claim through the shared
[result record](FOUNDATIONS.md#result-algebra), retaining its original
assurance outcome, evidence class and residual ambiguity. The predicate is
"claim C is supported on its declared subject/basis under its stated assurance
rule." Admissible evidence establishing that claim at the required evidence
altitude satisfies it, with tolerated ambiguity explicitly retained.
An observed counterexample is `falsified`; missing decisive support is `indeterminate`.
An unusable basis is `invalid_basis`, and an out-of-domain request is
`out_of_frame`. A proposed claim or an assessment not performed is never
`satisfied` by default. `observed`, `derived`, `interpreted` and `composed`
describe evidence provenance; they are not alternative success values.

constraints.statement: Bind declared purpose, interpreted predicate and actual source observations. Predictive adequacy is separate from a required construction outcome: predictive accuracy proves neither construction success nor predictive error its failure. Assurance should expose claim, observed/derived/interpreted/composed provenance, support surfaces, aspect-specific authority and remaining ambiguity/missingness. Shared result retains original assurance outcome, evidence class and ambiguity for 'claim C is supported on its declared subject/basis under its stated assurance rule.' Required-altitude admissible evidence satisfies with tolerated ambiguity retained; observed counterexample falsifies; missing decisive support is indeterminate; unusable basis invalid_basis; outside domain out_of_frame. Proposed/unperformed claims are never satisfied by default; provenance labels are not success aliases.

conditions: Every published entity cut.
exceptions: Outside a declared representation space, the boundary law is discharged semantically through Entity Cut Construction Law.

grounding.quote: Every published entity cut must be prompt-sufficient for reasoning.

constraints.statement: Every published cut must be prompt-sufficient for reasoning. At minimum it should expose identity, boundary, authority, state, evidence, treatment, covariance and ambiguity. Explicit blanket means the boundary where identity survives reinterpretation, not column enumeration; schemas evidence identity rather than constitute it. The test is interventional survival across adjacent-domain treatment, not structural membership. In a declared space, the boundary is a low-rank identity-preserving projection; overlays should expose both distributed evidence and recovering projection. Otherwise use semantic entity-cut law.

grounding.quote:
The attribute ledger is the accepted semantic record over which the entity cut
is projected. A single ledger state can support many different cuts at
different identities, boundaries, and context scopes; the cut records which
selection was taken, not that the ledger *is* the cut.

Every accepted object attribute should therefore be recoverable through:

- the object cut that contains it
- the attribute-ledger entries that justify it
- the assurance basis that accepted those entries
- the traced source surfaces that support the assurance

No object attribute should exist without ledger support. No ledger entry should
exist without assurance. No assurance should exist without traceable source.

constraints.statement: The materialized cut is a builder artifact, not raw source output. Source systems own operational truth; builder observes/comprehends; published cut is canonical object-level truth of the world-model layer; other projections derive from it. Artifacts should be versioned and explicitly superseded. The lineage is source→tracing→assurance→ledger→cut. Cut is immutable bounded identity/boundary selection over distributed ledger evidence with that evidence and acceptance basis, not mutable source or the ledger itself. One ledger state may support many cuts with different identities/boundaries/scopes; each records its selection. Every accepted attribute should be recoverable through its cut, supporting ledger entries, assurance and traced source; no attribute should lack ledger support, no entry assurance and no assurance traceable source. Geometric selection additionally invokes the declared-space construction law.

grounding.quote:

- I/O is allowed
- subscriptions to external sources are allowed
- imperative interop with the host platform is allowed (DOM, file system, native APIs)

- no I/O
- no subscriptions
- no imperative platform manipulation
